meaning_en: to overflow; to defect (to the other side)
definition_de: so voll werden, dass Flüssigkeit über den Rand fließt (die Badewanne läuft über; das bringt das Fass zum Überlaufen); auch: zur anderen Seite wechseln (zum Feind überlaufen). Untrennbar ist vor allem das Adjektiv 'überláufen' = zu voll mit Menschen (ein überlaufener Strand).
example_de: Während ich telefonierte, ist die Badewanne übergelaufen, und das ganze Bad stand unter Wasser.
example_en: While I was on the phone, the bathtub overflowed and the whole bathroom was under water.
visual_idea: Most typical collocation 'die Badewanne läuft über': water pouring over the rim and a flooded floor show über- (over the edge) as a clear result state; the shocked man with the phone in the doorway matches the sentence and adds humor. 'Zum Feind überlaufen' and the idiom 'das Fass zum Überlaufen bringen' are hard to picture.
image_prompt: a white bathtub in a small tiled bathroom filled to the brim, the tap still running, water spilling over the rim in a thin sheet and flooding the whole floor, a bath mat and a pair of slippers floating in the shallow water, a man in the open doorway holds a smartphone to his ear with his mouth open in shock, wide view from the corner
negative_prompt: text, letters, watermark, signature, caption, blurry, extra fingers, deformed hands, cluttered background, multiple panels
video_prompt: in a small tiled bathroom water runs from the tap into a full bathtub and starts spilling over the rim, spreading across the floor; a man on the phone appears in the doorway, stops and stares in shock; static wide camera
